cards.title: Sharp scalar positive regularization: universal tails, exact Pauli optimum and domain extensions
cards.scientific_scope: Incoming regularization programme plus separately attributed root-selected internal endpoint/domain/noncompact results. This draft does not assert external correctness, priority, efficient implementation or physical measurement capability.
cards.statement: For each m>=2 and R>0, one smooth radial strictly log-concave all-exponential scalar density positively regularizes every bounded self-adjoint m-tuple, on every Hilbert space, with ||sum u_j A_j||<=R|u|, and attains the largest eventual radial tail-envelope fixed offset b*=log[2/(R(m-1))]-1 in p(x)~C exp[-r/(2R)(log r+loglog r+b*)]. At that sharp offset the lower relative margin tends to zero in remote tails; the separate basic-endpoint epsilon sandwich must not be imported. Separately, for Mhat(t)=nuhat(t)exp(i t.sigma) for all three normalized Pauli observables, every radial positive scalar finite-variance law has covariance v I with v>=v*=23/9-2/[9(4K+2)], where K=integral_1^infinity h0, h0=1 on [0,2], and 2(s-1)h0'(s)+h0(s)+h0(s-2)=0 thereafter. Centering and rotations give tr Cov(nu)>=3v* for arbitrary scalar laws. Positive renewal attains v*; smooth spatial densities have the same infimum without attainment. Its multiplier obeys [3/(2080 sqrt2)]/(1+k^2)<=phi(k)<=2/(1+k^2), hence scalar convolution is H^s(R^3)->H^(s+2)(R^3) isomorphic. Separately, compact Banach-cone distributions admit precisely the proved open convex finite-MGF domains, and weighted-tempered (W) distributions admit the stated noncompact all-exponential criterion. As a separately identified classical boundary, an exact all-linear positive POVM representation with compact scalar noise exists for a bounded self-adjoint tuple on an arbitrary Hilbert space if and only if the operators commute pairwise. For each fixed valid exact representation, compact noise and compact outcome support are equivalent; commuting tuples may still have noncompact representations. This is an internally reconstructed short corollary of Uchiyama 1993 Theorem 7, with two direct internal proofs, not a historically new all-Hilbert-space theorem or foundational breakthrough.
assumptions: Endpoint: finite m, R>0, bounded self-adjoint tuple with the exact norm-ball contract; 0<epsilon<1 and the proof-specified sufficient scale.
Domain theorem: compactly supported real Banach-valued distribution, closed proper cone with nonempty interior, T(1)=e interior, and open convex D containing zero with transform interior on D.
Noncompact theorem: the full weighted (W) distributional seminorm hypothesis and T(1)=e; do not substitute arbitrary temperedness or all-noise exclusion.
Sharp offset: m>=2 and the exact universal radial eventual-envelope contract, with finite multiplicative constant; no uniform relative epsilon margin at that offset.

Pauli optimum: all three normalized coordinates, exact full scalar-convolution identity, positive scalar law/POVM and finite variance. Attainer is singular like 1/r; smooth subclass nonattainment is separate.

Compact-noise characterization uses the full exact all-linear multiplier identity and normalized weak POVM. Bounded noise in one direction plus all positive exponential moments in a second direction forces the corresponding commutator to vanish; finite Fourier-grid accuracy does not supply those tilted moments.
proof_spine: Endpoint Duhamel two-denominator estimate and analytic relative-error expansion; moment addendum and root/operator audits.
Anisotropic dual barrier, bounded primal mollification and exact moment-domain argument; separate finite-domain cross-audit.
Weighted distribution extension and noncompact positivity construction; retained scope correction and geometric-renewal counterexample.
Full transverse Clifford moment block plus separated exact second-order remainder attain the largest fixed offset; offset audit is explicit.
Positive renewal construction and positive adjoint dual certificate establish the Pauli optimum; full dual audit rather than finite LPs.
Root two-sided global Fourier bounds and separate Sol audit establish the Sobolev/inversion consequence.

Bounded first tilted outcome moment forces separated spectral blocks to vanish (root/Astra proof); an independent Phragmen-Lindelof/Liouville proof and exact Uchiyama 1993 Theorem 7 receiving comparison establish the known-machinery boundary.
cards.costs: Sufficient sharp-offset scales are extremely conservative (R=1,m=3: log10 L about 175, not a necessary lower bound). Charge acquisition, construction, preparation, finite-bit sampling and calibration. Fourier inverse amplification grows quadratically with cutoff, squared statistical amplification quartically. Raw Pauli report second moment v*+1≈3.533767 exceeds 3 for standard unbiased 3n. No complete implementation advantage follows.
cards.information_acquisition: Incoming prose is supplied; original producer ZIP absent. New internal proofs/reviews are separately attributable. Operator/margin data and physical measurement access are not acquired by theorem existence.
cards.obstruction: Sharp-offset relative lower margin vanishes remotely; finer corrections/prefactors remain unclassified. Weighted (W) cannot be replaced by arbitrary temperedness. The corrected noncompact example excludes all-exponential, not arbitrary probability noise. Optimal Pauli measurement is Blackwell equivalent to ordinary covariant spin and creates no extra quantum information. Exact compact scalar noise cannot regularize a noncommuting tuple under the complete all-linear identity. This does not rule out ordinary bounded joint measurements with weaker marginals or paid finite-output approximations.
cards.comparator: Weyl/Wigner, Husimi and known positive convolution remain prior machinery. Covariant spin is an information-equivalent Pauli comparator with lower standard-report second moment. Katkova-Vishnyakova, Vervaat and unresolved Diamond-Essen/fulltext comparisons prevent priority clearance. Uchiyama 1993 Theorem 7 already implies the all-Hilbert compact-noise characterization as a short corollary; historical novelty is not claimed for that theorem, and priority of the exact compact-smearing wording remains unresolved.
cards.missing_lemma: Independent external proof and exact historical-priority review; calibrated finite-bit sampling/measurement and complete matched costs. No optimizer uniqueness or finer tail law is inferred.
cards.next_decisive_step: Obtain external review and close precise priority gaps for the sharp tail, Pauli dual/Fourier chain, prescribed domains and weighted extension; pursue implementation only with calibrated full costs and informed comparators.

cards.title: Cause-conditioned clock certificates and information barriers for relative deadline tails
cards.scientific_scope: Supplied finite-generator mathematics and root-selected conditional certificates, countermodels and oracle-specific rare-tail obstructions. Finite checks remain distinct from analytic proof and acquired physical rates.
cards.statement: For a supplied finite stopped absorbing CTMC, retained initial support, positive cause committor c and p=mu c>0, endpoint Doob conditioning yields alpha_r^c=1+(Q_RI G c_I)_r/c_r and V_c=(2/p) sum_{i in I} eta_i (G c_I)_i. Conditional survival and directional-covariance bounds give the stated joint deadline/cause and finite-halfspace certificates. Original retained-state marginal and fixed-occupation weighted supermodularity survive in their exact time-error scope; general signed-reward variance has a counterexample to such an extension. Fixed finitely many moments/Laplace derivatives do not certify general relative deadline tails. In the specified rare-branch family p=M^-3, every mixture of scalar Esscher tilts retains the proved ordinary likelihood-ratio second-moment obstruction; this is not a lower bound on arbitrary analytic estimators or altered acquisition oracles. Weighted nonnegative cause-clock sums retain their exact fixed-weight supermodularity; worst-cause maxima do not. The explicit signed-reward counterexample raises residual variance from 6 to 8 on retaining a state.
assumptions: Finite supplied generator with the target stopped, retained initial support, finite discarded Green operator and exact reward/cause definitions.
Zero-committor states removed before division; conditional probability p and any requested tiny conditional survival require scope-matched relative accuracy.
Supermodularity fixes original occupation weights and concerns the stated unsigned time-error objective; general signed reward objectives are separate.
Finite-summary obstruction applies to the named bounded list of linear statistics; Esscher result applies to the stated scalar-tilt mixture and ordinary likelihood-ratio estimator class.
proof_spine: Stopped-clock martingale and Green identities; exact marginal and weighted supermodularity argument.
Endpoint Doob transform, conditional clock/covariance, common-row-clock incompatibility and joint probability bands.
Explicit signed-variance and finite-summary countermodels; phase-type interpolation and scalar Esscher-mixture obstruction with charged native acquisition.
cards.costs: Charge eliminated/reduced factorizations, fill, committor/reward solves, retained-state selection, precision and reduced distribution evaluation. Unknown rare branch probability p costs native gateway information; the stated observation lower bound is order p^-1 epsilon^-2 log(1/delta) on its exact oracle. Supplied normalizers, rates or selective channel control change the access contract.
cards.information_acquisition: Q, rewards, causes and p are mathematical supplied inputs unless separately measured. Conditioning does not acquire rare branches, physical rates or a Markov model. Exact tilt normalizers can reveal p and cannot be treated as free native observations.
cards.obstruction: One ordinary row clock need not preserve all cause-conditioned means; finite summaries and scalar Esscher mixtures do not generally repair relative rare tails. Signed-reward variance does not inherit the time-error supermodularity guarantee.
cards.comparator: Given the same complete generator and access, compare with exact positive-semigroup/phase-type computation, exponential-mixture formulas for the star family, matrix-exponential actions, exact Schur/renewal kernels and established Doob/state-dependent importance sampling. No end-to-end superiority established.

cards.next_decisive_step: Freeze exact conditional proofs and countermodels, retain acquisition-oracle distinctions, and test only a physically calibrated access route against equally informed full-semigroup and established importance-sampling comparators.

cards.title: Pressure-written states, post-extraction access and an annulus current/aging opportunity
cards.scientific_scope: Documentary acquisition and proposed instrumentation opportunity only. In-DAC pressure-release observations, extracted magnetic response and loaded post-extraction performance remain distinct physical states/contracts.
cards.statement: The acquired article and official SI do not establish a same-specimen post-extraction gross current/field/temperature/time capability. The reported in-DAC 151 K resistive onset, extracted magnetic onset near 140 K and shielding estimate at 70 K cannot be joined into that target. A mechanically released annulus, a closed external Maxwell-Ampere contour around a full cross-section, slit/calibration controls and separate material-age/current-decay variables specify a concrete opportunity to measure net winding current and aging. These established physical operations and ring-current prior art, including Tomita 2006, are not a demonstrated new Hg-1223 capability.
assumptions: Keep specimen identity, preparation, DAC/extraction state, temperature, magnetic field, current/load, age and measurement convention aligned.
Ampere-contour inference requires the full linked contour in the quasistatic regime, accounted threading currents, calibration and uncertainty; gross cross-section is measured conservatively.
Aging and current decay are varied independently; no unmeasured history carrier, trapping barrier, constitutive parameter or lifetime is supplied.
proof_spine: Published-main/official-SI documentary distinctions and exact acquisition/read receipts.
Stress/occupation arguments retain their narrow scope and explicit countermodels to overextension.
Annulus net-current identity, controls and two-time aging diagnostic, compared with existing ring methods.
cards.costs: Complete fabrication, pressure writing, cold recovery, mounting, full-contour readout, calibration, field/temperature control, loading, uncertainty, retention, losses and scaling costs remain unmeasured. Design calculations are not specimen performance.
cards.information_acquisition: Official SI acquired as external research, distinct from the absent producer ZIP. Commit exact URLs/hashes/read receipts and original analytical notes; exclude downloaded PDFs and whole copyrighted extracts. Joint post-extraction transport and microscopic memory carrier remain unacquired.
cards.obstruction: No acquired gross post-extraction J-B-T-time margin or demonstrated annulus preparation/recovery at the proposed regime. Onset, shielding, center-field signal or low-temperature creep does not supply the joint capability.

cards.title: Anisotropic distortion margin, strong critical storage and surviving weak-topology failures
cards.scientific_scope: Root-selected internal analytic consequence of an exact supplied Heat18 certificate plus separately reviewed elliptic/trace analysis. Exact nine-group arithmetic checks do not establish the analytic theorem externally or resolve general planar rank-one-convexity.
cards.statement: For A=[[a,b],[c,d]], u=a^2+c^2, v=b^2+d^2, j=ad-bc and G=3(u+v-2j)^2+(35/24)u^2+j^2-(5/2)ju, the selected certificate implies G-kappa|C A|^4 is quasiconvex with C A=(a-d,b+c) and kappa=3/16000. The reviewed Beurling/elliptic argument yields integral[G(B+D phi)-G(B)] >= gamma integral|D phi|^4 with gamma=1/2500000 on bounded Lipschitz domains, periodic rectangles and the stated zero-end-profile strips, uniformly in finite strip duration. Consequences are bounded-ball pairwise Lipschitz storage on strong W^(3/4,4)(T) modulo constants, and uniqueness/stability of the affine minimizer. Explicit weak lower and weak upper semicontinuity failures and finite-Fourier observation limits survive.
assumptions: Use the exact G coefficients and unchanged Heat18 input certificate; compactly supported or zero-trace gradient perturbations in the proof-specified W^(1,4) class.
Linear defect C is elliptic on actual gradients; the subtraction vanishes on the conformal plane and is not epsilon|A|^4.
Strong critical trace-space bounded balls, means/affine terms, strip geometry and required-supply storage conventions are exactly those in the selected proof.
proof_spine: Exact rank-two certificate subtraction and positive rational pivots; four-rotation average gives kappa=3/16000.
Quartic Bregman and Cauchy-Riemann/Beurling ellipticity yield gamma=1/2500000 and duration-independent gradient control.
Terminal unit-slab patch and adjusted-action mean handling establish bounded-ball strong storage continuity; explicit critical-scaling sequences retain weak failures.
cards.costs: Nine exact certificate groups were checked by author, Sol capital worker and root; these are arithmetic checks with separate analytic reconstructions. No explicit arbitrary-duration storage optimizer, evaluation formula, finite evaluation algorithm or physical implementation follows.
